title: Safety Net Rollup Checklist, Roadmap, and Release Notes (Sep 2026) - Draft
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, operational checklist + micro-calendar for the "safety-net" rollup release (backing service changes + routing policy tweaks) scheduled for the second week of Sep 2026. It pairs a short timeline with tactical handoffs, telemetry gates, comm templates, and a seed draft of release notes.

Context / Goals:
- Ship the routing-policy change that reduces cold-starts for small models by enabling local warm-pool priming.
- Keep user-facing latency P95 < 250ms and 5xx rate < 0.15% during rollout.
- Validate canary in two regions (us-west1, eu-west1) before global ramp.
- Minimize operator cognitive load: explicit checkpoints, simple rollback paths, and one-touch communications.

Scope (in-scope):
- Serving runtime change: warm-pool priming toggle + config flag change (infra PR 982).
- Traffic routing rule for fallback to smaller quantized model variant when latency SLOs breached.
- Observability: new telemetry tags, two eval prompt suites.

Out-of-scope:
- Model architecture changes, customer visible API changes, billing changes.

Who to loop in if X breaks:
- Latency spike / throughput regression: eng-sre on-call (primary: Marcus Chen, pager: @pager-ops), serving-runtime owners (Leila Gupta).
- Increased error rate (5xx): platform-engineering triage (Tomás Rivera), prod-support for customer-facing issues.
- Canary instability in EU region: infra-owner on-call + regional SRE.

Mini-calendar (UTC):
Day -2 (2026-09-10):
- 09:00: Final smoke run against staging, run eval suite (regression set A).
- 12:00: Lock PR and freeze changes; annotate release notes skeleton.
- 15:00: Deployment rehearsal dry-run: apply feature toggle to a sandbox cluster.

Day -1 (2026-09-11):
- 10:00: Readout meeting (30m) with SRE, serving-runtime, infra; confirm telemetry dashboards.
- 16:00: Post-readout checklist: pager rotas confirmed, Slack channel #release-orchestra pinned.

Day 0 (2026-09-12) - Canary start: us-west1
- 08:00: Preflight: run final health checks (see checklist). If any fail, abort and revert to Day -1 steps.
- 09:00: Deploy warm-pool toggle to 5% of traffic in us-west1 (canary).
- 09:15 - 10:15: Monitor telemetry. Primary metrics: P95 latency, 99th latency, error (5xx) rate, token-per-second throughput, CPU/GPU utilization.
- 10:30: If all gates pass for 60m, increase canary to 25%.
- 13:00: If stable for 2h, increase to 50% and hold for 1h.
- 16:00: If stable, mark us-west1 canary green and notify #release-orchestra.

Day 0 (same day) - Canary start: eu-west1 (staggered)
- 18:00 UTC: Repeat same ramp sequence in eu-west1 starting at 5%, hold same gate windows.

Day +1 (2026-09-13):
- 08:00: Global ramp to 80% across both regions over 3 steps (50% -> 80% -> 100%), holding 45m between increases.
- 14:00: Final monitoring window; if stability holds, flip toggle to default ON for all traffic at 17:00.

Staffing & communication plan:
- Lead coordinator (shift owner): Nora Alvarez (09:00-18:00 UTC coverage).
- SRE primary: Marcus Chen (pager contact), SRE secondary: Priya Singh.
- Serving runtime lead on-call: Leila Gupta.
- Infra fallback engineer: Tomás Rivera.
- Customer communications on watch: CS-runbook standby (notify if >10 customers affected).
- Slack channel for the release: #release-orchestra (use /standup templates).

Preflight checklist (must be green before Day 0):
- [ ] All PRs merged for this release (PR 982 + infra hotfixes).
- [ ] Staging smoke passed: smoke suite 12/12.
- [ ] E2E eval run: regression set A diff < 0.8% of metric X (quality gate).
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards (latency/error/throughput) created and saved.
- [ ] Alert thresholds pre-configured for temporary throttles.
- [ ] Canary routing policy ready; feature toggle ID: warm_pool_v2.
- [ ] Rollback playbook ready and circulated.
- [ ] Pager rota confirmed & phone numbers tested.
- [ ] Release notes skeleton drafted and uploaded to Confluence.

Telemetry gates (explicit acceptance criteria):
- Latency gate: P95 <= 250ms AND 99th <= 500ms for a 60m window after each ramp step.
- Error gate: 5xx rate does not increase by more than 0.05 absolute percentage points versus baseline.
- Throughput gate: total token/s within +/- 10% of baseline (no under-provision).
- Resource gate: GPU utilization stable; no unusual OOM or driver errors in logs.
- Quality gate: eval prompt set delta < 1.0% on intent-preserving metrics.

Automated alarms (to be armed pre-deploy):
- Alert LAT-CRIT: P95 > 350ms for more than 5 min.
- Alert ERR-FLUX: 5xx > 0.5% sustained for 3m.
- Alert THROTTLE-RISE: Token/s drop > 20% across the fleet in 10m.

Rollback decision matrix (condensed):
- Immediate rollback (full revert + toggle off) if any of:
  - LAT-CRIT fires and remains > threshold for 15m OR
  - ERR-FLUX fires with >0.2% absolute increase and customer impacting errors detected OR
  - Resource issues: memory OOM or GPU driver crash on >2 nodes in 10m.
- Soft rollback (reduce canary to 0% in problem region) if
  - Localized instability (only one region) and team wants more time.

Rollback runbook (one-touch):
1) Slack: @channel "Rolling back warm_pool_v2 in us-west1 due to ERR-FLUX; invoking rollback runbook."
2) Ops: run infra deploy revert-tag (stable): tag v2026-09-05-stable.
3) Toggle: set warm_pool_v2=false globally (CLI: config set warm_pool_v2 false --scope global).
4) Monitor metrics for 30m, comment on Jira REL-2048 with timeline and attached logs.

Communications (short templates):
- Slack (internal): "[Release] warm_pool_v2 canary started in us-west1 @09:00 UTC. Watching P95 and 5xx. Nora leading. Pager: Marcus. Link: CONFLUENCE:RELEASE-OPS-2026-09"
- Email (ops->CS): "Heads up: We are rolling out a routing/pool priming change that may affect latency briefly during ramp. We're watching; we'll update when the canary reaches 50% or earlier if we observe regressions."

Operational notes / sticky points to watch:
- Cold-start telemetry sometimes disguises as 429 spikes; watch for correlated logs with 'kv-cache-miss'.
- The priming path uses a short-lived prefill job; ensure job queue does not saturate.
- Watch for slowdowns on small-model warm pools (quantized variants) — these have different kernel selection paths.

Release notes (seed draft) - user-facing parts (short, for release page):
Title: Improved warm pool priming to reduce small-model cold starts
Release date: 2026-09-12 (target)
What changed:
- Enabled a new warm-pool priming mechanism that reduces the frequency of cold-start latency for smaller models. This change changes routing behavior to pre-warm model instances under certain short-lived traffic patterns.
Why this matters:
- Customers using short, latency-sensitive prompts should see fewer high-tail latencies. Typical improvement: median unchanged, P95 reduced by ~60–80ms in internal benchmarks.
How to know you’re affected:
- If you see occasional latency spikes > 300ms on short prompts (<64 tokens) previously, you should see fewer occurrences.
- No API key or SDK changes required.
Known issues and caveats:
- There is a small risk of transient errors during rollout in corner-case traffic shapes; we have a staged ramp and rollback plan.
- Some debug-grade telemetry tags are new; if you rely on internal tags, review the observability notes.

Operational checklist (post-release, first 24–72h):
- 0–1h: Confirm canary region metrics and roll to 100% if green.
- 1–6h: Keep on-call rotation in place; check-in update at 6h.
- 6–24h: Run extended regression eval (regression set B, longer prompts).
- 24–72h: Draft post-deploy note summarizing anomalies and action items; add to REL-2048.

Telemetry query snippets (for quick copy):
- Error rate (5xx) by region (CloudMetrics): "sum(rate(http_5xx_count[5m])) by (region) / sum(rate(http_request_count[5m])) by (region)"
- P95 latency (rolling 15m): "histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[15m])) by (le, region))"
- Prefill job queue depth: "prefill_queue_length{job="warm_prefill"}"

Notes to self / loose todos (informal):
- Re-run perf microbench against quantized-v2 on smaller hardware — results looked noisy last run. (Leila)
- Follow up with console team to make the warm_pool toggle visible in the UI; quick link would help CS. (Marcus)
- Add one more smoke prompt to staging that reproduces prior cold-start spike. Save as smoke/coldstart-01.

Attachments & artifacts (where to look):
- Confluence page: CONFLUENCE:RELEASE-OPS-2026-09 (detailed rollout + runbook)
- Jira ticket: REL-2048 (intent, rollouts, postmortem)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/982 (warm-pool priming changes)
- Slack thread: #release-orchestra (search "warm_pool_v2")

Quick retrospective prompts (post-mortem starter):
- What surprised us during rollout?
- Did telemetry gates catch everything we cared about? If not, what was missing?
- Could we have reduced operator steps by automating any of the manual holds?
- Was our comm cadence adequate for CS and customers?

---
This is a working draft. Put TODOs and inline comments in the doc Slack thread or comment in Confluence. If you are listed as a collaborator, please add brief sign-off next to your name when your preflight item passes.
